Δεύτερος ὁ Ῥουβὴμ, καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ. Καὶ τρίτοι μὲν πάλιν οἱ ἐξ ἐλευθέρας. Εἶτα μετὰ τούτους ἕτεροι τρεῖς, οἱ ἐκ θεραπαινῶν, περὶ ὧν εἴρηται τὸ, «Ἔσχατοι ἐξαροῦσιν.» Ἆρ' οὐκ ἐναργὲς καὶ οὐδαμόθεν ἐνδοιαστὸν, ὅτι προτετίμηται καὶ προεισκέκληται τοῦ πρωτοτόκου τὸ δεύτερον, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὸ ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ τῶν ἐκ δουλείας τὸ ἐλεύθερον ἐν πίστει; Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἡγοῦνται διὰ τὸν ἐξ Ἰούδα Χριστόν· οἱ δὲ κατόπιν ἔρχονται μόλις, καὶ ὡς ἐν δευτέρᾳ τέθεινται τάξει. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθότατα ἔφης· καί σε τῆς οὕτω λεπτῆς ἀγχινοίας ἐπαινέσαιμι.
pass_a_gloss: [cont. quotation] by their divisions (τάγματα).' You see that Judah and those with him are ranked first (προτέτακται), and have the chosen (ἀπόλεκτον) place toward dawn (ἠώ) and south (νότον)? For in light (φωτί) are those in Christ, and in the spirit/Spirit boiling/fervent (τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες). Second Reuben and those with him. And third again those from the free woman (ἐλευθέρας). Then after these other three, those from maidservants (θεραπαινῶν), about whom is said 'Last they will set out (ἔσχατοι ἐξαροῦσιν).' Is it not evident (ἐναργές) and from nowhere doubtful (ἐνδοιαστόν), that the second has been honoured before (προτετίμηται) and called in before (προεισκέκληται) the firstborn, that is, the [people] in Christ, and the free in faith (ἐν πίστει) [before] those from slavery (δουλείας)? For the ones lead (ἡγοῦνται) because of the Christ from Judah; the others come behind (κατόπιν) scarcely (μόλις), and as in second order (τάξει) have been placed. PALL.: Most rightly you said; and I would praise you for such fine (λεπτῆς) sagacity (ἀγχινοίας).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …by their divisions’ (Numbers 2:25–31). Do you see that Judah and those with him are placed first, and hold the chosen place toward the dawn and the south? For those who are in Christ are in the light, and fervent in the Spirit (Romans 12:11). Second comes Reuben and those with him. Third, again, are the sons of the free woman. Then after them come three others, the sons of the maidservants, of whom it is said, ‘They shall set out last’ (Numbers 2:31). Is it not plain, and in no way open to doubt, that the second, that is, the people in Christ, has been honoured above the firstborn and called in ahead of it, and so have those who are free in faith above those who come from slavery? For the one group leads because of Christ, who is from Judah; the others only barely follow behind, and have been placed, as it were, in the second rank.
Palladius: You have spoken most rightly, and I would praise you for such fine sharpness of mind.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens by closing the Numbers 2:25-31 quotation begun at the end of §39 (LXX 2:31 κατὰ τάγμα αὐτῶν; Cyril has the plural τάγματα). 'Toward the dawn and the south': Judah camped on the east (Numbers 2:3); Reuben, not Judah, held the south (2:10). Cyril appears to pair east/dawn with 'light' and south (νότος, the warm wind) with 'fervent', which explains the double phrase; translated as written. τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες is a verbal echo of Romans 12:11 and is cited; 'in the light' may echo 1 John 1:7 or Ephesians 5:8 but is too general to cite. 'Christ, who is from Judah' recalls Hebrews 7:14 (ἐξ Ἰούδα); left uncited as a commonplace of the argument already made in §37. τοῦ πρωτοτόκου τὸ δεύτερον: 'the second [has been honoured above] the firstborn', with the genitive of comparison governed by προ- in both perfects; τῶν ἐκ δουλείας τὸ ἐλεύθερον ἐν πίστει rendered with plural persons for natural English. The old English row for §40 carried an extra closing doxology ('To God be the glory...') that is not in this source block; nothing was added here.

changes: προτετίμηται καὶ προεισκέκληται now governs both pairs (second over firstborn; free in faith over those from slavery); earlier text dropped 'called in ahead' from the second pair
μόλις: 'come behind, and barely' -> 'only barely follow behind'
Refs checked: Num 2:25-31, Num 2:31, Rom 12:11 (τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες) correct; east/south pairing is Cyril's own, kept and noted
